snippet:
Pylon is an x402 API gateway that lets AI agents discover and pay for APIs with cryptocurrency in a single HTTP request. Third-party providers list their APIs on Pylon and get paid instantly — no sales team, no billing system, no invoices.
## What You Get
- **85% revenue share** — you set the price, Pylon takes only 15%
- **Instant USDC payments** on Base — no net-30, no invoicing
- **Zero sales/billing overhead** — agents discover your API automatically via Pylon's capability registry
- **Built-in payment verification** — x402 protocol handles payment before your code runs
- **MCP + REST distribution** — agents find you through both protocols
---
## Prerequisites
- **Node.js 18+** (or any runtime — the template uses Node/Express)
- **A deployed API endpoint** (or something you want to turn into one)
- **A wallet address** on Base for receiving USDC payouts

Once deployed, register your API with the Pylon gateway:
```
# Using the included registration script
node register.js \
--name "Your Tool Name" \
--description "What your API does" \
--url "https://your-app.fly.dev/api/your-tool" \
--method GET \
--cost 0.01 \
--keywords "keyword1,keyword2,keyword3"
```
Or submit directly:
```
curl -X POST https://api.pylonapi.com/register \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
"id": "your-tool",
"name": "Your Tool Name",
"description": "What your API does in one sentence.",
"keywords": ["keyword1", "keyword2"],
"providerEndpoint": "https://your-app.fly.dev/api/your-tool",
"method": "GET",
"cost": "$0.01",
"inputSchema": {
"input": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Input parameter" }
},
"outputType": "application/json",
"provider": {
"name": "Your Company",
"wallet": "0xYourWalletAddress",
"url": "https://yoursite.com",
"contact": "you@yoursite.com"
}
}'
```

title: Pylon | Airbyte Docs
snippet:
## Prerequisites​
- A Pylon API token created by an Admin under **Settings > Integrations & dev > API tokens**. Choose a role that can read the data you plan to sync. If the token acts as a user or bot, it inherits that identity's current role and permissions. Pylon tokens have no separate scopes. For creation steps, see [Pylon's authentication guide](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication#create-an-api-token).
- Access to Tags for the source connection check, plus access to each selected stream and its parent stream. A successful connection check does not verify access to every stream.

Enter only your **API Token**, without the word `Bearer` or surrounding spaces. The connector adds the authentication header to all requests to the Pylon API.
Select **Region** to match your Pylon tenant and API token. **US** (the default) uses `https://api.usepylon.com` with tokens prefixed `pylon_api_`. **EU** uses `https://api.eu.usepylon.com` with tokens prefixed `pylon_api_eu_`. For older tokens without a prefix, choose the region where your Pylon tenant is hosted. Existing configurations without Region continue to use US.

title: Pylon Integration
snippet:
## Requirements
- A Pylon workspace on a plan with API access (Professional, Advanced or Enterprise).
- A Pylon **Admin**. Only Admins can create API tokens.
- To use the Update user role action, the token must have the **Admin** role.
### **Required keys**
To connect this integration, we require the following:
- A Pylon API token
- The region where your Pylon workspace is hosted (US or EU)
## How to Generate the Required Values
**Step 1: Create an API token**
1. In Pylon, go to **Settings >> Integrations & dev >> API tokens** and click **Create API Token**.
2. Enter a **Name**, for example **Torii**.
3. Leave **Act as user or bot (optional)** empty, so the token has its own identity.
4. Pick a **Role**. The **Admin** role works. A lower role may work if it can read users. The Admin role is required only for the Update user role action.
5. Click **Create** and copy the token.
**Important**
Pylon shows the token only once, so copy it before closing the window.
When a user is deactivated, Pylon deletes every token that user created or that acts as that user. Create the token from a long-lived admin or bot account.
**Step 2: Find your region**
Use the region where your Pylon workspace is hosted. EU tokens start with **pylon_api_eu_**. If your token does not start with that prefix, your workspace is most likely in the US region.
| **Where your workspace is hosted** | **Region to select in Torii** |
|---|---|
| US | US (api.usepylon.com) |
| EU (token starts with pylon_api_eu_) | EU (api.eu.usepylon.com) |
For more details see Pylon's guide: [Authentication](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication).

title: Pylon MCP | Pylon
snippet:
- **Server URL (US):** `https://mcp.usepylon.com`
- **Server URL (EU):** `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com`
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.0 or an API token. Actions are performed as the signed-in user or the token's identity, with that identity's current role and permissions.
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (stateless; no server-side sessions).

#### API token
Use an existing API token for headless workers, scripts, or MCP clients that support custom authorization headers. You don't need a separate MCP token or an interactive sign-in.
1. Configure your client with your workspace's regional MCP URL.
2. Include this header on every MCP request:
Replace `<API_TOKEN>` with the token value. Use `https://mcp.usepylon.com` for US workspaces and `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com` for EU workspaces; the token must belong to the same region.
A token with its own identity uses the role assigned to that identity. A token linked to a teammate or bot uses that user's current role and permissions. The identity must have **MCP Access**, and each tool still requires the permissions for its operation. Any IP allowlist configured on the token also applies to MCP requests.

The authenticated user or token identity needs the **MCP Access** [permission](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/platform/roles-and-user-management#member-permissions-2) to connect. The standard Member and Admin roles include this permission. Each tool also requires the permissions for its operation. Access follows the same scoping as the Pylon dashboard — the MCP cannot return data that the authenticated user cannot already see, or perform writes that the authenticated user cannot already write in the UI.

When no other tool does what you need, AI tools can run operations from the [Pylon REST API](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api) directly. Each call runs as the authenticated user, so the operation's own permission checks apply, just as they do in the Pylon dashboard.
